purpose: Teach: 戰/燈/會/茵/繭/狭間/のっとっ/云い

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、旧字「戰」、つまり戦時史の表記研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on old-character forms—specifically the historical records of wartime writing conventions, didn't you?
lines.style: Measured, genuinely curious. Slightly formal academic register. Opens with attention-seeking directness, then settles into thoughtful pacing. Listening for the answer with steady presence.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、旧字「燈」、つまり灯の照明文化史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote my paper on the old character for 'light'—specifically the cultural history of illumination in historical documents.
lines.style: Quiet certainty. Respectful to the teacher. A touch formal, careful with his words. Slight pause before answering, as though checking his accuracy. Even cadence, no rush.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、旧字「會」、つまり会合の文書史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you explored old-character forms in your paper—specifically the documentary history of gatherings and written records, yes?
lines.style: Thoughtful, inviting. Warm academic curiosity. Slightly softer than the first question, as though she's noticing something in his pattern of answers. Leans in with genuine interest.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、敷物の茵、つまり茵席の民俗誌を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I focused my paper on woven floor mats—specifically the folklore and material culture of traditional seating practices.
lines.style: Steady and direct. A slight shift in his tone, as though he's moved to different ground. Still formal, but with a touch more conviction. Cleaner line delivery.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、絹糸の繭、つまり養蚕の繭の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, I see you wrote about silk culture—specifically the agricultural and historical research on sericulture and cocoons, correct?
lines.style: Reflective and warm. The pacing slows slightly, as if she's noticing the breadth of his interests. Gentle confirmation in her tone. Genuine delight at the scope.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、谷の狭間の地理研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote about geographical research—specifically the study of narrow valleys and the spaces between ridgelines.
lines.style: Steady, grounded. His voice carries a quiet confidence here. No hesitation. Direct and complete. A hint of engagement with the subject matter itself.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、古文書「のっとっ」、つまり「則っ」の用法を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you tackled classical documents in your paper—specifically the usage patterns of an older grammatical form, didn't you?
lines.style: Gently probing now. Warmth underneath. Her voice carries the cadence of someone piecing together a larger picture. Patient, attentive to his responses.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、古文の云い、つまり「言い」の旧形の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, my paper examined classical grammar—specifically the archaic forms and historical usage of what we now write as a modern verb construction.
lines.style: Clear, assured finish. His tone brightens slightly, engaged with the material. Precise, without being stiff. A natural conclusion to his thought.
